title: Replace sign_in_context_reset_test.dart's source-text-matching 'wiring' assertions with real call-chain verification
why: The 'wiring' group (4 tests) reads sign_in_controller.dart / account_picker_screen.dart as raw text with File.readAsStringSync() and asserts substring presence (e.g. 'routerProvider).pinGuard.lock()' appears somewhere after another substring). This proves the token exists in the file — including inside a comment, a dead branch, or an `if (false)` — not that the reset actually runs during a real sign-in. A refactor that renames a local variable, extracts the same call into a helper, or reorders it outside the funnel would either false-fail (token literally moved) or false-pass (token still present but now unreachable) without any real Riverpod/router state ever being observed. The file's own 'runtime semantics' group shows the better pattern is available (it drives the real PinGuard/activeTutoredProfileSelectionProvider primitives directly) — it just never chains them through an actual signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle call.
recommendation: Replace the source-grep assertions with an end-to-end check: seed a tutored selection + authenticated PIN scope, drive SignInController.signInWithEmail/signInWithGoogle (as sign_in_controller_test.dart and the sign_in_*_throws_test.dart files in this batch already do with a stub router), and assert the real providers were cleared afterward — the same technique the 'runtime semantics' group in this file already uses for the primitives themselves.
acceptance_criteria: No test in this file reads a .dart source file as text to assert behavior.
Commenting out (not deleting) the _resetSessionContextForFreshSignIn() call inside _navigateAfterSignIn makes the corresponding test fail red.
